intro: Localization quality depends on geometric overlap. Pairwise intersection over union compares boxes of different sizes without treating touching edges as positive area.
task: Compute pairwise geometric overlap and distinguish touching edges, containment, and zero-area boxes.
requirements: boxes and other are finite matrices shaped (N,4) and (M,4), with coordinates [xmin,ymin,xmax,ymax]. Zero-area boxes and empty matrices with four columns are allowed.
Require xmax>=xmin and ymax>=ymin. Return an (N,M) float array of intersection area divided by union area.
Use continuous coordinates without a pixel +1 correction. Define IoU 0 for zero union, including two identical zero-area boxes.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Clip intersection side lengths
hints.body: Disjoint boxes can produce negative raw lengths, which must become zero before multiplication.

hints.title: Broadcast both box axes
hints.body: Compare each row from the first matrix with every row from the second.

explanation: IoU normalizes intersection area by the combined area covered by either box. It is symmetric and stays in [0,1] for valid boxes.
Continuous-coordinate geometry has no pixel-inclusive +1 term. Declaring the coordinate convention prevents a subtle disagreement between otherwise similar detection implementations.
